title: Keep the quote feed answering while it backs off

blocks.text: The trading desk's monitoring page asks every market-data feed for its `status()` once a second. When a feed loses its connection, its own thread calls `reconnect()`, which backs off between attempts, for up to two minutes when the exchange is down. That is exactly when the desk most wants to see the feed's status, and it is when the monitoring threads stop getting answers. At shutdown, `close()` should make a reconnect give up, and today shutdown waits out the back-off.
`QuoteFeed` keeps its state under its own monitor, and `reconnect()`, `status()` and `close()` stay `synchronized`. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/QuoteFeed.java`:

items: `pause(long millis)`: the back-off between two attempts, called from inside `reconnect()`;
`close()`: closes the feed, and a reconnect that is backing off gives up at once.

blocks.text: When you're done, `status()` answers during a back-off of any length, and `close()` ends a back-off in progress. About seven lines in total.
The tests run `reconnect()` on a thread of its own, with back-offs of a few milliseconds and of two minutes.

cases.says: a feed whose first two attempts fail backs off between them and connects on the third
a feed that is already closed makes no attempt
status() answers while reconnect() is in a two-minute back-off
close() during a two-minute back-off makes reconnect() give up at once

origin.section: A Waiting Thread Keeps Every Lock but the One It Waits On

concepts: A thread that sleeps or waits for anything but wait() inside synchronized keeps the monitor, so every other caller is BLOCKED for as long as it waits.
Object.wait() releases the monitor of the object it is called on while it waits, so other threads can enter.
A waiting thread leaves WAITING only when another thread acts on it (notify, unpark, an interrupt) or its time runs out; setting a field it would check later wakes nothing.
